Key observations from the test image:
- Bright **green stems** that remain moist and green
- **Mature/dry tan-brown pods** already dried out
- Stark contrast between green stems and mature pods
- Soil/field background — late-season plant

This strongly suggests **Green_stem_disorder** (green stems persisting while pods mature). Let me also check Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus which can cause green stems, plus confirm with reference images.
The Green_stem_disorder reference is an **excellent match** — green stems with mature dry pods, same field setting. Let me check a few more to confirm no other disease fits.
Diaporthe and Anthracnose both show dark/brown stems — completely different. Let me view more references to reach the 12-image minimum.
None of these match — SDS shows leaf necrosis, Phytophthora shows wilting/browning, Dwarf Mosaic shows stunted green plants, White Mold shows fluffy mold. Let me view 4 more to complete the minimum.

All 12 reference images viewed. None of the leaf-disease candidates (Septoria, Frogeye, Cercospora, Brown Stem Rot) resemble the test image at all.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: Bright green, moist stems alongside fully matured/dry tan-brown pods — the defining hallmark of Green_stem_disorder
- Green_stem_disorder reference: Nearly identical — green stems + dry mature pods, same field setting, same close-up perspective
- All other candidates show leaf lesions, stem browning, fluffy mold, or systemic wilting — none match
- Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (another green-stem cause) shows leaf mottling and is transmitted by beetles — the test image shows no leaves or mottling, just the green-stem-vs-dry-pod contrast
